md_description: This workflow models the generation and analysis of data from traditional medicinal plants used in nutraceutical formulations. It covers plant material preparation, extraction, chromatographic isolation, structural spectroscopy, and cellular bioactivity assays, producing raw signals and derived results that can be integrated to identify active compounds and support standardization and health-benefit claims for nutraceutical products.

medicinal_plant_material.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included only intrinsic identity/origin fields for the collected plant biomass and excluded any preparation, extraction, capture, signal, or derivative/result fields. Because this is the root biological material in the workflow, the most useful metadata are what plant it is, where and when it was collected, what plant part was sampled, and basic provenance/voucher information needed to trace the material and support reproducibility. I avoided duplicating downstream preparation or assay details and kept identifiers generic so they do not conflict with already_generated fields (none were provided).

md_schema.descr: Accepted scientific name of the medicinal plant biomass at collection time, e.g. 'Curcuma longa'. Record the taxon used for the study material, not the extract or any processed fraction.
Common or local name used by collectors or source documentation for the plant biomass, e.g. 'turmeric' or a vernacular name. Record as supplied to preserve provenance.

Plant organ or tissue collected as starting biomass, recorded at collection time and typically reported as leaf, root, rhizome, bark, stem, flower, seed, or whole_plant. This describes the source material before any drying or extraction.

Free-text collection site description or locality string for the source plant biomass, e.g. village, reserve, farm, district, and country. Record the original field collection location, not laboratory location.
Date when the plant biomass was collected from the field or source repository, in ISO format YYYY-MM-DD. This anchors provenance for the starting material.
Name of the person or team that collected the plant biomass. Use the name as recorded in field notes or accession records.
Voucher specimen identifier or herbarium accession for the collected plant, if available, e.g. 'HNU-2024-015'. Use a stable string that can link the biomass to a preserved reference specimen.

Method used to identify the plant taxon at collection time, such as morphologic_identification, herbarium_comparison, dna_barcoding, or expert_verification. Record the provenance of the species-level identification, not a laboratory assay.
Source status of the collected biomass at the time of sampling, indicating whether it came from a wild population, cultivated stock, or market-supplied material.
Permit, ethics, or access-and-benefit identifier associated with lawful collection of the plant biomass, if applicable, e.g. collecting permit number. Record as a stable string exactly as issued.

dried_plant_material.reasoning: This is an Entity node representing the prepared plant biomass after cleaning and drying, so I included only intrinsic preparation-state metadata for the material itself. I focused on properties that define the dried starting material for downstream extraction: the drying method, drying endpoint, residual moisture, storage conditions, and mass/yield of the prepared biomass. I excluded upstream collection provenance because that belongs to the medicinal_plant_material node, and I excluded extraction or analytical parameters because those belong to downstream process/capture nodes. I also avoided repeating identity fields already generated for the root material unless they specifically describe the dried state.

md_schema.descr: Method used to dry the collected plant biomass before extraction, recorded at the preparation step, e.g. air_drying, oven_drying, freeze_drying, shade_drying. Capture the actual drying approach applied to this material.

Temperature in degrees Celsius used during drying when a controlled-temperature method was applied, measured during the preparation step, typically in the range of 20-80 C depending on method. Record the set or average drying temperature for this dried material.
Total duration in hours spent drying the biomass, measured from the start to the end of the drying step. Typical values range from a few hours to several days depending on method and tissue type.

Residual moisture content of the dried plant material after preparation, expressed as percent wet weight or equivalent laboratory moisture basis used in the study. Measure at the end of drying; typical dried biomass values are often below 15 percent.
Mass of the plant material after cleaning and drying, in grams, measured at the end of the preparation step before extraction. Record the actual mass available for downstream solvent extraction.
Condition used to store the dried biomass prior to extraction, recorded after drying and before downstream processing, such as room_temperature_dry, refrigerated, frozen, or desiccated_storage.
Number of days the dried plant material was stored before extraction, measured from completion of drying to initiation of extraction. Use this to capture pre-extraction holding time.

Text description of the physical size state after any cutting, grinding, or milling performed on the dried material before extraction, e.g. 'coarse powder' or 'passed through 40 mesh'. Record the prepared form used for downstream extraction.

Indicates whether visible soil, debris, or non-target plant matter was removed during the preparation step before drying and extraction. Use this only to document the cleaning state of the dried starting material.

crude_plant_extract.reasoning: This is an Entity node describing the extracted material itself, so I included intrinsic extract properties and provenance of the extract state rather than the extraction protocol. I focused on fields that downstream users need to understand what the crude extract is: solvent identity as reflected in the extract, extract concentration/solid content, yield, appearance, storage, and batch identity. I excluded extraction-process parameters such as temperature, time, ratio, agitation, or equipment because those belong on the extraction_process node, and I avoided repeating raw plant provenance fields from upstream entities.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for this crude plant extract batch, e.g. 'CE-2024-001'. Use this to link the extract to its source material and downstream fractionation results.

Primary solvent or solvent system represented by the crude extract, e.g. methanol, ethanol, water, ethyl_acetate, or hydroalcoholic mixture. Record the solvent composition associated with this extracted material, not the extraction procedure details.

Crude extract yield expressed as percent of starting dried biomass mass, calculated for the extract batch after solvent removal. Typical values vary widely by plant and solvent; record the final yield associated with this extract entity.
Mass of the recovered crude extract in grams, measured after solvent removal and before aliquoting or fractionation. Record the actual recovered material mass for this batch.

Concentration of the crude extract solution or reconstituted stock, in mg/mL, measured when the extract is prepared for storage or downstream assay. Use this only if the crude extract is stored or handled in solution form.
Physical state of the crude extract at the time it is recorded, such as dried_residue, viscous_oil, semi_solid, or lyophilized_powder. Describe the entity itself, not the procedure used to obtain it.

Temperature in degrees Celsius at which the crude extract is stored before fractionation or testing, measured during the post-extraction holding period. Typical values include -20, 4, or room temperature depending on stability.
Solvent or vehicle used to keep the crude extract in solution during storage, if applicable, e.g. DMSO, methanol, ethanol, or water. Record the medium in which this extract entity is maintained.

Free-text visual description of the crude extract batch at the time of recording, e.g. 'dark green powder' or 'amber viscous residue'. Capture observable physical characteristics of the extract entity.
Number of aliquots or subsamples prepared from this crude extract batch for downstream fractionation or assays. Record the count of discrete stored portions derived from this extract entity.

fractionated_extracts.reasoning: I corrected the prior schema by removing the colliding field storage_temperature_celsius because it was already generated in an earlier DAG step and must not be repeated. The remaining fields stay within the Entity territory of fractionated_extracts: batch identity, fraction indexing, collection mode, elution window, recovered mass, reconstitution concentration, physical state, appearance, and enrichment note. I kept out process-level chromatographic settings and downstream analytical outputs, and I preserved only non-duplicative material properties needed to identify and reuse the fraction entity.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the set of chromatographically separated fractions, e.g. 'FRAC-2024-01'. Use this to link fractions back to the source crude extract and forward to purification or analysis.
Ordinal number or label assigned to an individual fraction within the batch, recorded at the time of collection from the chromatographic separation, e.g. 1, 2, 3 or 'A', 'B'.
How the fraction was collected from the separation run, such as time_based, peak_based, or fixed_volume. Record the operational collection scheme used to generate this fraction entity.

Description of the elution interval or retention window from which the fraction was collected, e.g. '12-15 min' or 'peak 3'. Capture the fraction's chromatographic origin window, not the instrument settings.

Recovered mass of the individual fraction in milligrams, measured after collection and solvent removal if applicable. Typical values depend on scale and fraction richness; record the mass for this fraction entity.
Concentration of the fraction when reconstituted for storage or downstream testing, in mg/mL. Measure this at the point the fraction is prepared for later use.
Physical state of the fraction at the time it is recorded, such as dried_powder, viscous_residue, or solution. Describe the fraction itself rather than the separation procedure.
Free-text visual description of the fraction, e.g. 'yellow powder' or 'dark brown viscous oil'. Capture observable appearance of the fraction entity for later traceability.

Brief qualitative note on the apparent enrichment of candidate active compounds in the fraction, based on the collected material and prior screening, e.g. 'alkaloid-rich' or 'phenolic-enriched'. Record only the material-level observation, not the analytical method.

isolated_compounds.reasoning: This is an Entity node for purified compounds, so I included only intrinsic compound identity, purity, provenance, and physical-state fields that describe the isolated material itself. I avoided repeating any already_generated field names or semantics, including storage_temperature_celsius from earlier entity steps, and I excluded process details from purification or downstream spectroscopy/bioassay nodes. The resulting fields help a downstream user identify what the compound is, how pure it is, how much was isolated, and whether it is stable or archived for later analysis.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the purified compound entity, e.g. 'IC-001'. Use a stable string that links this isolated compound to fractionation, structure assignment, and assay records.

Provisional or tentative name assigned to the purified compound at the isolation stage, if any, e.g. 'compound A' or a literature-based tentative name. Record the working name used before final structural confirmation.

Estimated purity of the isolated compound expressed as percent, measured after purification and before structural analysis or bioassay. Typical purified isolates often fall in the range of 70-100 percent.
Recovered mass of the purified compound in milligrams, measured at the end of the isolation workflow before aliquoting or storage. Record the actual amount obtained for this compound entity.
Identifier of the fraction or fractions from which this compound was isolated, e.g. 'FRAC-2024-01-3'. Use this to preserve the link from fractionated material to purified isolate.
Physical state of the purified compound at the time it is recorded, such as crystalline_solid, amorphous_solid, oil, or solution. Describe the isolated entity itself, not the purification protocol.
Free-text visual description of the purified compound, e.g. 'white crystalline solid' or 'yellow oil'. Capture observable appearance of the isolated entity for traceability.

Brief note on apparent stability of the isolated compound during handling and storage, e.g. 'light-sensitive', 'air-stable', or 'degrades on standing'. Record intrinsic handling stability observations for the entity.
Current status of the purified compound in the workflow, such as archived, consumed_for_analysis, or available. Record the entity's current availability for downstream spectroscopy or assay.

plant_preparation.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I kept only process-operational fields for plant preparation and removed the colliding drying-related field ids that were already generated earlier in the DAG. To preserve the node's semantics without duplicating those fields, I replaced them with non-colliding preparation parameters that still describe how the biomass was cleaned, reduced, and judged ready for extraction. I excluded upstream plant identity/provenance and downstream dried-material properties, which belong to other nodes.

md_schema.descr: Method used to clean the incoming plant material during preparation, recorded at the start of the process, e.g. rinsing, brushing, manual_debris_removal, or solvent_wipe. Capture the operational cleaning approach applied before drying.

Method used to reduce particle size during preparation, such as cutting, chopping, grinding, milling, or sieving, recorded as part of the process. This describes how the biomass was made extraction-ready.
Target particle size or mesh specification achieved during preparation, e.g. 'powder', '40 mesh', or '1-2 mm pieces'. Record the intended size state established by the process.
Mass of starting plant material processed in a single preparation batch, in grams, measured at the beginning of the process. Record the batch size handled by this preparation run.
Percent of starting plant mass retained after cleaning and size reduction, calculated at the end of the preparation process. Typical values depend on debris removal and moisture loss.
Name or identifier of the researcher or technician who carried out the preparation step. Record who performed the process operation.
Overall quality assessment of the prepared plant material immediately after processing, such as acceptable, rework_required, or rejected. Record the process output quality indicator for this step.

Brief description of the equipment or tools used in plant preparation, e.g. 'knife and grinder', 'bench mill', or 'sieving set'. Record the main apparatus used in the process, excluding downstream extraction equipment.

Qualitative note describing the observed reduction in moisture or freshness during preparation, e.g. 'fully air-dried' or 'slightly pliable after drying'. Record the process observation rather than a measured endpoint already captured elsewhere.
Indicates whether visible debris or non-target plant material was removed during preparation before extraction. Use this to document whether an explicit cleaning/removal step was performed.

extraction_process.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I kept only extraction operation parameters, equipment identity, and a quality indicator. I removed the colliding operator field and avoided any output-material properties that belong to the crude_plant_extract entity. The selected fields describe how the extraction was executed, with enough detail for reproducibility while staying within the process layer and respecting previously generated field names.

md_schema.descr: General extraction approach used on the prepared plant biomass, recorded at the process step, e.g. maceration, soxhlet, reflux, ultrasound_assisted_extraction, or percolation. Describe how soluble metabolites were isolated from the biomass.

Solvent or solvent mixture used during extraction, recorded as the actual system applied to the biomass, e.g. water, ethanol, methanol, hydroalcoholic mixture, or aqueous_acetone. This describes the process reagent, not the extracted material.

Ratio of dried plant biomass mass to solvent volume used during extraction, typically expressed as g:mL or equivalent. Record the ratio set for this extraction run, as it strongly affects yield and selectivity.
Total duration in hours for the extraction operation, measured from solvent contact start to process completion. Typical laboratory extractions range from minutes to many hours depending on method.

Temperature in degrees Celsius maintained during extraction, measured at the process stage when temperature was controlled or monitored. Typical values range from room temperature to solvent reflux temperatures.
Agitation or stirring speed in revolutions per minute used during extraction, measured when the extraction was mixed mechanically. Record this only if agitation was part of the process.
Percent yield of extract recovered from the starting dried biomass, calculated at the end of the extraction process before any fractionation. Typical values vary by plant matrix and solvent system.
Model designation of the extraction apparatus used for the process, e.g. Soxhlet setup model, shaker model, or extraction vessel system. Record the hardware identity for reproducibility.
Overall quality assessment of the extraction run immediately after completion, such as acceptable, rework_required, or failed. Record the process output quality indicator for this step.

chromatographic_fractionation.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the operating conditions and agent/hardware details of the chromatographic separation, plus a process-level quality indicator. I avoided fields about the resulting fractions themselves because those belong on the fractionated_extracts entity, and I excluded any previously generated field names such as process_operator_name. The selected fields are the minimum needed to reproduce the fractionation setup and understand how the separation was executed.

md_schema.descr: General chromatographic mode used for fractionation, recorded at the process step, e.g. normal_phase, reverse_phase, ion_exchange, size_exclusion, or flash_chromatography. Describe the separation principle applied to the crude extract.
Stationary phase material used for the chromatographic fractionation, e.g. C18 silica, silica gel, Sephadex, or resin type. Record the actual separation medium used in the process.

Mobile phase composition or gradient program used during fractionation, recorded as the solvent system applied in the chromatographic process, e.g. water/acetonitrile with formic acid or hexane/ethyl acetate gradient.
Flow rate in milliliters per minute used during chromatographic separation, measured at the process stage. Typical values depend on column scale and system type.
Total run time in minutes for the chromatographic fractionation, measured from sample injection to completion of the separation run.
Column or separation temperature in degrees Celsius maintained during fractionation, measured when temperature control was used. Record the operating temperature for the separation run.
Detector wavelength in nanometers used to monitor eluting compounds during fractionation, recorded at the process step when UV or related detection was active.
Model designation of the chromatographic instrument used to perform the fractionation, e.g. HPLC, UPLC, or flash chromatography system model. Record the hardware identity for reproducibility.
Identifier of the researcher or technician who ran the chromatographic fractionation. Use a stable string identifier rather than a personal name when required by the data system.
Overall quality assessment of the fractionation run immediately after completion, such as acceptable, rework_required, or failed. Record the process output quality indicator for this step.

compound_purification.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the purification workflow parameters and operation-level agent/hardware details needed to reproduce isolation of single compounds from fractions. I avoided fields that describe the purified compound itself because those belong to the isolated_compounds entity, and I excluded any duplicate or already-generated field names from prior steps. The resulting schema captures purification strategy, solvent system, run conditions, yield, and process quality for the purification step.

md_schema.descr: Purification technique used to isolate individual compounds from fractions, recorded at the process step, e.g. preparative_hplc, recrystallization, solid_phase_extraction, or repeated_chromatography. Describe the isolation strategy applied to the fraction.
Solvent or solvent mixture used during purification, recorded as the actual system applied in the process, e.g. water/acetonitrile, methanol, hexane/ethyl_acetate, or buffer-based eluent.

Total duration in hours for the purification operation, measured from start of purification to collection of the purified compound. Typical values vary from less than an hour to multiple days depending on method.
Temperature in degrees Celsius maintained during purification, measured at the process stage when temperature control was used. Record the operating temperature for the isolation run.
Recovered mass of the purified compound in milligrams, measured at the end of the purification process before downstream analysis. Use this as the process output yield for the isolated material.
Target or acceptance purity percentage for the purification run, defined at the process stage as the minimum purity sought before the compound is accepted for downstream identification or testing.
Identifier of the researcher or technician who carried out the purification step. Use a stable string identifier for the operator responsible for the process.
Model designation of the purification instrument used, such as preparative HPLC system model, flash cartridge platform, or related hardware. Record the hardware identity used for purification.
Overall quality assessment of the purification run immediately after completion, such as acceptable, rework_required, or failed. Record the process output quality indicator for this step.

chromatography_capture.reasoning: This is a Capture node, so I kept only session-level measurement configuration and hardware details needed to interpret the chromatographic acquisition. I removed the colliding field instrument_model because it was already generated earlier in the DAG, and I avoided output-file properties that belong on the chromatogram_signal node. The remaining fields describe the capture session identifier, hardware identity, detector setup, column configuration, and acquisition software, which are the minimum details needed to reproduce the measurement context.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the chromatographic measurement session, e.g. 'LC-SESSION-001'. Use this to link the instrument configuration to the resulting chromatogram signal.
Manufacturer of the HPLC or UPLC instrument used for chromatographic capture, recorded as the hardware vendor at the measurement session. Example: Agilent, Waters, Shimadzu, Thermo Fisher.
Serial number of the chromatographic instrument, recorded to uniquely identify the hardware used in the capture session. Use the exact manufacturer-issued identifier when available.
Detector type used during chromatographic capture, such as UV, DAD, PDA, FLD, or MS-based detection when coupled to the LC system. Record the active detector configuration for the session.

Detector wavelength in nanometers used to monitor the chromatographic run, measured during the capture session when a UV or related detector was active. Typical values are in the ultraviolet to visible range.
Injection volume in microliters used for the chromatographic measurement session, recorded at the instrument setup stage. Typical values are in the low microliter to tens of microliters range.
Type or designation of the LC column installed for the capture session, e.g. C18 reverse-phase column, silica column, or chiral column. Record the column used by the instrument during acquisition.

Column dimensions used for the chromatographic session, typically recorded as length x internal_diameter with units, e.g. '150 x 2.1 mm'. Capture the physical column format configured for measurement.

Version of the instrument acquisition software controlling the chromatographic capture session, e.g. vendor software version number. Record the configured software environment used to acquire the data.
Overall assessment of the chromatographic capture session immediately after acquisition, such as acceptable, rerun_required, or failed. Record the session-level quality indicator for the measurement.

chromatogram_signal.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I included only raw data artefact metadata: file format, file size, dimensions, acquisition completeness, and storage location. I excluded capture settings such as detector type or instrument model because those belong to the chromatography_capture node, and I excluded peak tables or interpreted features because those belong to downstream processing and derivative nodes. I also avoided reusing any prior field names that could collide with earlier DAG steps.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the raw chromatogram file, e.g. 'CHROM-RAW-001'. Use this string to link the file to the capture session and processing records.
Technical file format of the raw chromatographic readout, recorded when the data file is saved or ingested, e.g. .raw, .cdf, .mzml, .txt, .csv, or vendor-specific binary format.
Size of the raw chromatogram file in bytes, measured from the stored digital artefact after acquisition. Typical values vary widely by run length and vendor format.
Number of time points or scans represented in the raw chromatogram, recorded from the digitized signal file. Use this to describe the temporal resolution of the artefact.
Number of recorded channels in the raw chromatographic file, such as multiple wavelengths or detector channels. Record the channel count present in the artefact.
Indicates whether the chromatogram file is complete and readable at the time of ingestion, such as true for intact files or false for truncated/corrupted files.
Storage path or URI where the raw chromatogram file is located, e.g. file server path, object store URI, or repository location. Record the retrieval location of the signal artefact.

Total chromatographic run length in minutes encoded in the raw file, typically matching the acquisition window from injection to end of recording. Record the observed duration represented by the artefact.

Estimated baseline noise level of the raw chromatogram, as stored or estimated from the artefact, used as a technical quality descriptor of the raw signal. Record the noise metric if available from the file or ingestion pipeline.
Checksum or digest of the raw chromatogram file, e.g. MD5 or SHA-256 string, used to verify file integrity during storage and transfer.

chromatogram_processing.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the computational peak-integration workflow: the software used, version/repository information, key integration parameters, and a process-level quality flag. I did not include raw signal file properties because those belong to chromatogram_signal, and I did not include the resulting peak table fields because those belong to peak_table. I also avoided previously generated field names and kept the schema limited to what is necessary to understand and reproduce the peak integration step.

md_schema.descr: Name of the chromatography processing software used to integrate peaks and convert raw chromatograms into analyzable tables, e.g. vendor integration suite or third-party analytics package. Record the software that performed the process.
Version of the chromatography processing software used for peak integration, recorded at the time of processing. Use the exact version string to support reproducibility.

Repository, vendor package source, or distribution channel for the processing software, e.g. official vendor site, GitHub repository, or lab-managed package registry. Record where the software came from.

Algorithm or integration strategy used to define chromatographic peaks, recorded during processing, e.g. automatic_thresholding, manual_curation, baseline_to_baseline, or valley_to_valley. Describe how peaks were identified from the raw chromatogram.
Indicates whether baseline correction was applied before or during peak integration, recorded as a process parameter of the computational workflow.
Indicates whether signal smoothing was applied before peak calling, recorded as a computational preprocessing setting in the chromatography processing step.
Numerical threshold used by the integration algorithm to define peak boundaries or detect peaks, recorded at processing time. Use the native unit or normalized scale reported by the software.
Minimum peak area accepted during peak integration, measured or set in the processing software to filter out noise peaks. Record the cutoff used for inclusion in the peak table.
Indicates whether manual review or curation was needed after automated peak integration, used as a computational workflow quality indicator.
Overall quality assessment of the peak integration result, such as acceptable, rework_required, or failed. Record the process output quality indicator for this step.

peak_table.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only computed result fields describing the peak table itself: table identity, row/feature counts, retained dimensions, summary statistics, and quality indicators. I excluded raw chromatogram properties and peak integration parameters because those belong to upstream signal and process nodes, and I avoided any fields already generated elsewhere. The schema is limited to what a downstream user needs to understand the derived chromatographic feature table and reuse it in integration analysis.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the computed peak table, e.g. 'PEAKTAB-001'. Use this string to link the table to the specific chromatogram processing result.
Identifier of the raw chromatogram signal from which this peak table was computed, used to trace the derivative back to the source artefact.
Number of chromatographic features or peaks retained in the computed table after integration and filtering, measured as the row count of the derivative result.
Minimum retention time in minutes represented in the peak table, corresponding to the earliest integrated chromatographic feature in the derived result.
Maximum retention time in minutes represented in the peak table, corresponding to the latest integrated chromatographic feature in the derived result.
Total summed peak area across all retained chromatographic features in the computed table, used as a summary measure of signal abundance in the derivative result.
Technical format of the computed feature table, e.g. csv, tsv, xlsx, parquet, or database table export. Record the serialization format of the derivative artefact.
Status of any candidate feature annotation in the peak table, such as unannotated, tentative, or partially_annotated. Record the scientific interpretation state attached to the computed features.
Overall quality assessment of the computed peak table, such as acceptable, rework_required, or failed. Record the derivative output quality indicator for this result.

spectroscopy_capture.reasoning: This is a Capture node, so I kept only the spectroscopy session and instrument configuration fields needed to interpret the measurement. I removed the colliding acquisition_software_version field because it was already generated for an earlier DAG step, and I continued to exclude sample identity, output spectral file properties, and downstream structural interpretation. The remaining fields describe modality, hardware identity, acquisition mode, spectral window, and a few key session settings.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the spectroscopic measurement session, e.g. 'SPEC-SESSION-001'. Use this to link the capture configuration to the resulting spectral signal.
Spectroscopy modality used to record the compound signature, recorded at the capture step, such as NMR, MS, or IR. This identifies the measurement principle used by the instrument.
Manufacturer of the spectrometer used for the capture session, recorded as the hardware vendor at measurement time. Example vendors include Bruker, Thermo Fisher, Agilent, Shimadzu, or PerkinElmer.
Model name or number of the spectrometer used, e.g. 'Avance III', 'Orbitrap Exploris', or an IR instrument model. Record the specific hardware configuration used for this capture.
Serial number of the spectrometer used in the capture session, recorded to uniquely identify the hardware instance. Use the exact manufacturer-issued identifier when available.
Acquisition mode used for the spectroscopy session, such as 1d, 2d, full_scan, targeted_scan, or transmission depending on modality. Record the active data acquisition mode for the capture.
Measured spectral window for the capture session, expressed as chemical shift range in ppm for NMR, mass-to-charge range for MS, or wavenumber range for IR. Record the active acquisition window used.

Resolution or spectral resolution setting used during capture, recorded as the instrument setting relevant to the modality, e.g. spectral resolution in ppm, Da, or cm^-1. Use the native unit reported by the instrument.
Temperature in degrees Celsius of the sample during spectroscopic capture, measured or controlled at acquisition time when applicable. Typical values depend on modality and sample handling.

spectral_signal.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I included only raw spectral artefact metadata such as file format, size, dimensionality, and technical integrity/storage fields. I excluded spectrometer settings and acquisition software details because those belong to spectroscopy_capture, and I excluded any structural interpretation because that belongs to spectral_processing and structure_assignment. I also avoided any field names that could collide with earlier signal metadata by focusing on spectroscopy-specific raw file properties.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the raw spectral file, e.g. 'SPEC-RAW-001'. Use this string to link the file to the spectroscopy session and downstream processing records.
Technical file format of the raw spectral readout, recorded when the data file is saved or ingested, e.g. .fid, .raw, .mzml, .spc, .jdx, or vendor-specific binary format.
Size of the raw spectral file in bytes, measured from the stored digital artefact after acquisition. Typical values vary widely by modality and file type.
Number of spectral dimensions represented in the raw file, such as 1 for 1D spectra or 2 for 2D NMR data. Record the dimensionality of the artefact.
Number of sampled points, scans, or intensities contained in the raw spectral file, recorded from the digitized signal artefact. Use the native count that reflects file resolution.
Storage path or URI where the raw spectral file is located, e.g. file server path, object store URI, or repository location. Record the retrieval location of the signal artefact.
Checksum or digest of the raw spectral file, e.g. MD5 or SHA-256 string, used to verify file integrity during storage and transfer.
Estimated noise level of the raw spectral artefact, used as a technical quality descriptor of the captured signal. Record this if available from the file or ingestion pipeline.
Estimated baseline drift or instability in the raw spectral signal, recorded as a technical quality metric for the artefact. Use the instrument- or pipeline-reported value when available.
Indicates whether the raw spectral file is complete and readable at the time of ingestion, such as true for intact files or false for truncated/corrupted files.

spectral_processing.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the interpretation workflow used to convert raw spectral data into structural assignments, plus the software/analyst context needed for reproducibility. I excluded raw spectral file properties because those belong to spectral_signal, and I excluded the resulting structure annotations because those belong to structure_assignment. I also avoided any previously generated process field names that could collide across the DAG.

md_schema.descr: Interpretation strategy used to assign structural features from the spectral data, recorded at the process step, e.g. manual_annotation, automated_assignment, library_matching, or expert_review. Describe how the spectra were interpreted to produce structural conclusions.

Name of the software used to interpret the spectral data, e.g. vendor analysis suite or third-party spectral assignment package. Record the software that performed or supported the interpretation process.
Version of the spectral analysis software used during interpretation, recorded at the time of processing. Use the exact version string for reproducibility.
Repository, vendor source, or distribution channel for the spectral analysis software, e.g. official vendor site, GitHub repository, or lab package registry. Record where the software came from.

Minimum confidence threshold used when assigning structural features from spectra, recorded as a process parameter if the software uses confidence scoring. Typical values are on a 0 to 1 scale or a percentage scale depending on the tool.
Indicates whether a human analyst had to manually review or edit automated spectral assignments during the interpretation process.

Name or identifier of the spectral reference library used for matching or annotation, if applicable, e.g. in-house library or public spectral database. Record the resource used to support interpretation.
Identifier of the analyst or curator who interpreted the spectral data, if manual or hybrid review was performed. Use a stable identifier rather than a free-text personal name when possible.
Overall quality assessment of the spectral interpretation result, such as acceptable, rework_required, or failed. Record the process output quality indicator for this step.

structure_assignment.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only computed structural-result fields: table identity, source signal link, assigned identity summaries, confidence, and quality indicators. I excluded spectroscopy capture settings and spectral interpretation workflow parameters because those belong upstream to spectroscopy_capture and spectral_processing, and I excluded any fields already generated elsewhere. The selected schema describes the derived structure-annotation table itself so a downstream user can reuse or audit the compound identity assignments.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the computed structure assignment table or record set, e.g. 'STRUCT-001'. Use this string to link the derived annotations to the spectral interpretation result.
Identifier of the raw spectral signal from which this structure assignment was derived, used to trace the derivative back to the source artefact.
Label or provisional compound name assigned in the structure table, e.g. 'compound 1' or a tentative natural product name. Record the identity annotation produced by the derivation.
Molecular formula inferred for the isolated compound from spectral interpretation, recorded as a derived identity attribute, e.g. 'C20H30O'.
Broad structural class assigned to the compound, e.g. flavonoid, alkaloid, terpenoid, phenolic_acid, or steroid. Record the derived chemical class if available.
Confidence score for the structural assignment, recorded as produced by the interpretation workflow. Typical scales are 0 to 1 or 0 to 100 depending on the tool used.
Short summary of how the structural assignment was derived, e.g. library match, NMR dereplication, MS fragmentation, or combined evidence. Capture the computed annotation pathway for the result.
Overall quality assessment of the structure assignment result, such as acceptable, rework_required, or failed. Record the derivative output quality indicator for this table.
Technical format of the derived structure assignment artefact, e.g. csv, tsv, xlsx, json, or database_table. Record how the computed result is serialized for storage or exchange.

cell_assay_preparation.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the assay setup parameters, reagent/cell handling details, culture conditions, and the executing agent/hardware context needed to reproduce the preparation of the bioactivity assay. I excluded the cell culture entity properties because those belong on cell_assay_sample, and I excluded raw readout or normalized response outputs because those belong on bioactivity_capture, bioactivity_signal, and bioactivity_metrics. I also avoided previously generated field names and kept the schema focused on how the assay was prepared for antioxidant and anti-inflammatory testing.

md_schema.descr: Name of the cell line or primary cell type prepared for the assay setup, recorded at the process step, e.g. RAW264.7, HEK293, THP-1, or primary macrophages. Describe the cellular system being prepared for testing.

Source or origin of the cells used in assay preparation, e.g. ATCC, vendor catalog number, in-house isolation, or donor-derived primary cells. Record the provenance of the cellular material used in the process.

Passage number of the cultured cells at the time of assay preparation, measured when the cells are seeded or conditioned for testing. Typical values are lab-specific and should be recorded exactly as used.
Number of cells seeded per well or equivalent assay unit during preparation, measured at setup time. Record the density used to establish the assay system before compound exposure.
Well-plate or culture format used for assay preparation, e.g. 96-well, 48-well, 24-well, or chamber_slide. Record the physical assay container format used in the process.
Culture medium used during assay preparation, e.g. DMEM, RPMI-1640, or phenol_red_free medium. Record the medium in which cells were prepared before bioactivity testing.
Percentage of serum in the culture medium during preparation, measured at the time of seeding or equilibration. Typical values are 0-20 percent depending on the assay design.

Incubation temperature in degrees Celsius used to equilibrate cells and reagents during assay preparation, typically around 37 C for mammalian cells. Record the controlled culture temperature applied before testing.
CO2 percentage used in the incubator during assay preparation, typically around 5 percent for standard mammalian cell culture. Record the controlled atmosphere used for the process.
Description of how isolated compounds were diluted for assay exposure, e.g. serial two-fold dilution or fixed concentration series. Record the preparation scheme for test compound dosing.

cell_assay_sample.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included only intrinsic properties of the prepared cell culture system itself, avoiding any field names already generated earlier such as cell_line_name, cell_source_description, and passage_number. I focused on sample state and provenance attributes that remain specific to the living assay system: viability, confluence, growth state, spatial placement, contamination status, and treatment-readiness descriptors. I excluded preparation protocol details because those belong to cell_assay_preparation, and I excluded capture or signal properties because those belong downstream to bioactivity_capture and bioactivity_signal.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the prepared cell culture system used in bioactivity testing, e.g. 'CELLASSAY-001'. Use this string to link the living cell sample to the assay preparation and capture records.

Viability of the prepared cell culture system at the time of assay setup, expressed as percent live cells. Measure this immediately before or at the start of bioactivity testing; typical acceptable values are often above 80 percent.
Estimated confluence of adherent cells at the time the assay system was prepared, expressed as percent surface coverage. Record this for adherent cell assays where confluence affects response.
Growth phase or cellular state of the prepared culture, such as exponential, confluent, quiescent, or differentiated. Record the physiological state of the living assay system at preparation time.
Plate well or location identifier for the prepared cell culture system, e.g. A1, B12, or row/column coordinate. Use this to track the spatial placement of the living sample within the assay plate.
Number of freeze-thaw cycles experienced by the cells prior to assay preparation, if applicable. Record this as a provenance/stability property of the living cell sample.
Mycoplasma testing status of the cell culture system at preparation time, such as negative, positive, or not_tested. Record the contamination status relevant to the prepared biological sample.
Brief description of the culture condition state immediately before assay exposure, e.g. rested, serum_starved, stimulated, or washed. Record the biological readiness state of the living cell system.

Type of plate well surface or insert format used for the prepared cell system, e.g. tissue_culture_treated, low_attachment, or transwell. Record the physical culture environment associated with the sample.
Whether the prepared cell system was freshly prepared, temporarily held, or cryopreserved before assay use, recorded as a sample-state property of the living system.

bioactivity_capture.reasoning: This is a Capture node, so I included only the measurement session and instrument configuration for the bioactivity readout, not the cell sample properties, reagent identities, or processed assay outputs. The schema focuses on the plate reader or imaging system identity, acquisition settings, detection mode, plate setup, and session context needed to interpret the captured assay responses. I excluded raw file properties because those belong on bioactivity_signal, and I avoided previously generated field names to reduce DAG-wide collisions.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the bioactivity measurement session, e.g. 'BIOASSAY-SESSION-001'. Use this to link the capture configuration to the resulting assay signal.

Manufacturer of the plate reader or imaging system used for the bioactivity capture session, recorded as the hardware vendor at measurement time. Example vendors include BioTek, Tecan, Molecular Devices, or Olympus.
Model name or number of the bioactivity capture instrument used, e.g. plate reader or imaging system model. Record the specific hardware configuration used for this session.
Serial number of the bioactivity capture instrument, recorded to uniquely identify the hardware used in the capture session. Use the exact manufacturer-issued identifier when available.
Detection mode used during the bioactivity capture session, such as absorbance, fluorescence, luminescence, or imaging. Record the active measurement principle used by the instrument.
Excitation wavelength in nanometers used when fluorescence or related optical detection was active during capture. Record the instrument setting used for measurement, if applicable.
Emission wavelength in nanometers used when fluorescence detection was active during capture. Record the instrument setting used for measurement, if applicable.
Integration or exposure time in milliseconds used by the capture instrument during assay measurement, recorded at acquisition time. Typical values depend on detector type and signal intensity.
Physical plate format used for the bioactivity capture session, e.g. 96-well, 384-well, or imaging plate. Record the assay container type installed for measurement.
Name of the software controlling the bioactivity capture instrument, e.g. vendor plate reader software or imaging acquisition package. Record the software used to acquire the assay data.

bioactivity_signal.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I included only raw assay artefact metadata and removed the colliding storage-location field. The remaining fields describe the raw bioactivity file itself—its format, size, modality, dimensionality, and technical integrity—without stepping into capture settings or derived biological interpretations. I also avoided fields already generated elsewhere in the DAG to keep the schema collision-free.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the raw bioactivity readout file, e.g. 'BIO-RAW-001'. Use this string to link the file to the capture session and downstream analysis records.
Technical file format of the raw assay readout, recorded when the data file is saved or ingested, e.g. .csv, .txt, .tiff, .png, .nd2, or vendor-specific binary format.
Size of the raw bioactivity file in bytes, measured from the stored digital artefact after acquisition. Typical values vary widely by assay type and imaging content.
Type of raw assay measurement represented in the signal file, such as absorbance, fluorescence, luminescence, or image-derived. Record the measurement modality encoded in the artefact.
Number of wells or assay positions represented in the raw file, recorded from the digitized assay artefact. Use this to describe the spatial scope of the signal data.
Number of time points represented in the raw assay file when the experiment is kinetic, recorded from the raw artefact. Use 1 for endpoint assays with a single readout.
Number of image frames or fields of view recorded when the assay signal is image-based. Record this only for imaging-derived readouts.
Checksum or digest of the raw bioactivity file, e.g. MD5 or SHA-256 string, used to verify file integrity during storage and transfer.
Technical quality assessment of the raw bioactivity signal at ingestion time, such as complete, partial, or corrupted. Record the integrity state of the artefact before processing.
Number of image or detector channels encoded in the raw assay artefact when relevant, recorded from the file metadata or acquisition export. Use this only for multiplexed or imaging-based signals.

bioactivity_processing.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the computational normalization workflow, its software context, key parameters, and a process-level quality indicator. I excluded raw assay file properties because those belong to bioactivity_signal, and I excluded the resulting normalized metrics because those belong to bioactivity_metrics. I also avoided any previously generated field names, including signal-storage style metadata, so the schema stays within the processing territory only.

md_schema.descr: Normalization or analysis strategy used to convert raw assay readouts into comparable response values, recorded at the process step, e.g. percent_control, z_score, background_subtraction, or fold_change. Describe how the raw bioactivity measurements were computationally transformed.

Name of the software used for normalization and summarization of assay readouts, e.g. vendor analysis package or third-party statistics tool. Record the software that performed the bioactivity processing.
Version of the bioactivity processing software used during normalization, recorded at the time of analysis. Use the exact version string to support reproducibility.
Repository, vendor source, or distribution channel for the processing software, e.g. official vendor site, GitHub repository, or lab package registry. Record where the software came from.

Description of the control condition used for normalization, such as vehicle_control, untreated_control, positive_control, or combined_control. Record the reference condition used to compute relative responses.

Indicates whether outlier filtering was applied to raw assay values before or during normalization, recorded as a process parameter. Use this to document whether extreme wells or images were excluded.
Method used to combine technical or biological replicates during processing, e.g. mean, median, or robust_m_estimator. Record how replicate-level readouts were summarized.
Minimum value of the normalization scale after processing, e.g. 0 for percent control or a lower bound of a transformed metric. Record the lower bound used in the summary transformation.
Maximum value of the normalization scale after processing, e.g. 100 for percent control or an upper bound of a transformed metric. Record the upper bound used in the summary transformation.
Overall quality assessment of the processing result, such as acceptable, rework_required, or failed. Record the process output quality indicator for this step.

bioactivity_metrics.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only computed bioactivity-result fields that describe the metric table itself: identity, source signal link, assay domain, summary metric values, and quality/format descriptors. I excluded raw assay capture settings and processing parameters because those belong to the bioactivity_capture and bioactivity_processing nodes, and I avoided any field names that would collide with earlier DAG steps. The schema is limited to the derived activity metrics needed for ranking compounds and supporting nutraceutical claims.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the computed bioactivity metrics table or record set, e.g. 'BIO-METRICS-001'. Use this string to link the derived metrics to the assay processing result.
Identifier of the raw or processed assay signal from which this metrics table was derived, used to trace the derivative back to the source readout.
Biological endpoint represented by the derived metric set, such as antioxidant, anti_inflammatory, or combined. Record the activity domain summarized by the computed results.

Computed percent inhibition or response suppression value derived from the assay readout, typically expressed as a percentage relative to control. Record the main activity summary metric when available.
Computed half-maximal inhibitory concentration from the assay results, reported in the concentration unit used by the study, e.g. uM or ug/mL. Record the derived potency estimate when calculated.
Unit associated with the IC50 value, such as uM, nM, or ug/mL, recorded alongside the derived potency metric for clarity.

Derived effect-size statistic summarizing the strength of the bioactivity response relative to control, as computed by the analysis workflow. Use the statistic returned by the assay pipeline, e.g. fold_change or standardized effect.
Rank or ordinal category assigned to the assay result after computation, used to compare compounds within the same bioactivity panel. Record the derived prioritization label if available.
Confidence score for the derived metrics, recorded as produced by the analysis workflow. Typical scales are 0 to 1 or 0 to 100 depending on the method used.
Technical format of the derived metrics artefact, e.g. csv, tsv, xlsx, json, or database_table. Record how the computed results are serialized for storage or exchange.

integrative_analysis.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the computational integration workflow, its software context, key decision parameters, and a process-level quality indicator. I excluded any input-specific result fields because those belong to peak_table, structure_assignment, and bioactivity_metrics, and I excluded the final ranked compound list because that belongs to candidate_active_compounds. I also avoided previously generated field names and kept the schema focused on how the integrative analysis was performed.

md_schema.descr: Computational strategy used to combine chromatographic features, structural assignments, and bioactivity metrics, recorded at the process step, e.g. rule_based_ranking, weighted_scoring, machine_learning, or evidence_matching. Describe how the multi-omics style evidence was integrated.

Name of the software or analysis environment used for the integrative analysis, e.g. R script, Python pipeline, or vendor analytics package. Record the tool that performed the compound prioritization process.
Version of the integration software or pipeline used during the analysis, recorded at the time of processing. Use the exact version string to support reproducibility.
Repository, vendor source, or distribution channel for the integration software, e.g. official repository, GitHub, or lab-managed package registry. Record where the analysis code or tool came from.

Description of how chromatographic, structural, and bioactivity evidence were weighted in the integrative scoring step, e.g. equal_weighting, bioactivity_prioritized, or structure_prioritized. Record the decision rule applied to combine evidence types.

Minimum evidence threshold required for a compound to be considered in the integrative ranking, recorded as the rule or numeric cutoff used by the analysis workflow. Typical thresholds may be score-based or support-count based.

Brief description of the criteria used to flag compounds as promising candidates, e.g. high bioactivity, strong structural confidence, and chromatographic abundance. Record the operational rule used for prioritization.
Indicates whether consistency across replicates or independent assays was required before a compound could be prioritized, recorded as a process parameter.
Identifier of the analyst or data scientist responsible for the integrative analysis, if human oversight or review was part of the process. Use a stable identifier when available.
Overall quality assessment of the integrative analysis result, such as acceptable, rework_required, or failed. Record the process output quality indicator for this step.

candidate_active_compounds.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only the computed ranked-result fields that describe the candidate list itself: table identity, links back to the integrated analysis, ranking scores, prioritization labels, and result-format/quality descriptors. I excluded all upstream process parameters and source-specific fields because those belong to the input derivations and the integrative_analysis process, and I avoided previously generated field names to prevent collisions. The schema is aimed at supporting downstream selection of promising nutraceutical compounds and traceability back to the integrated evidence.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the computed candidate active compounds list or result table, e.g. 'CAND-001'. Use this string to link the ranked output to the integrative analysis result.
Identifier of the integrative analysis result from which this candidate list was derived, used to trace the derivative back to the source computation.
Rank assigned to each candidate compound in the prioritized list, with lower numbers indicating higher priority. Record the derived ordering used for nutraceutical selection.

Composite score used to prioritize compounds based on structure, abundance, and bioactivity evidence, recorded as produced by the ranking model or rule set. Typical scales may be normalized or arbitrary.
Derived label indicating candidate status, such as high_priority, medium_priority, low_priority, or rejected. Record the summary class assigned by the integration workflow.

Short computed or curated rationale summarizing why the compound appears in the candidate list, e.g. strong bioactivity with high confidence structural annotation. Record the reason attached to the derivative result.

Derived summary of chromatographic abundance or relative abundance used in candidate ranking, such as normalized peak area or relative enrichment. Record the abundance signal as represented in the final result table.
Technical format of the candidate list artefact, e.g. csv, tsv, xlsx, json, or database_table. Record how the computed result is serialized for storage or exchange.
Overall quality assessment of the candidate list output, such as acceptable, rework_required, or failed. Record the derivative output quality indicator for this result.

Brief note on the compound's relevance to nutraceutical standardization or health-benefit claims, as captured in the final ranked output. Record only the downstream prioritization context, not the original assay details.
